body.x: Procyan (CEO Lee Jae-yoon) announced its participation in CES 2024, which will be held in Las Vegas, USA, from January 9th (Tuesday) to 12th (Friday) local time.

Procyan is an AI Edutech company aspiring to bridge global disparities in math education. The company aims to enhance learners’ math skills through its adaptive learning service. To achieve this vision, they developed a “Math Calculation Engine,” allowing learners to solve unlimited math problems tailored to their skill levels.

Learners can use the “Math Calculation Engine” for iterative learning to address weaknesses. The AI math tutor, combined with this engine, diagnoses the learner’s problem-solving methods and engages in a mutual conversation to guide them on areas for improvement and which math concepts to understand. Through this process, learners identify their weaknesses and, via conceptual understanding, enhance their math skills quickly.

This adaptive math learning service named “Solgit” was launched for free in web and mobile versions in August this year. It is undergoing technical enhancement by integrating the virtual human into “Solgit.”

Regarding B2C, Procyan primarily targets middle and high school students worldwide. One of the reasons they focus on providing math education in over 104 languages globally is because the Fourth Industrial Revolution demands mathematical knowledge to drive innovation in STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, Mathematics) fields.

body.x: Regarding this, a Procyan representative explained, “Connecting basic math concepts and applying them to equations is a way for numbers and mathematics to communicate in the era of the Fourth Industrial Revolution. However, surviving in the STEM era becomes more challenging, causing the learner to lose momentum in understanding mathematics. The future world will likely be divided between those proficient in mathematics and those who are not. While the learner must catch up with this trend, the global gap in math education is widening faster. This is the philosophical reason behind our creation of ‘Solgit.’”

‘Solgit’ is based on Procyan’s Math Calculation Engine and a generative AI chat model. It executes a math problem recommendation algorithm using specialized natural language processing technology for mathematical sentences. ‘Solgit’ engages in conversations and interactions with users, providing personalized problems. Additionally, it utilizes data from users’ problem-solving processes to offer detailed explanations focused on the concepts causing difficulty.

Procyan has launched ‘Solgit’ in an MVP format for free on Korea’s web and mobile app. They’ve received investments in the Seed round. They rigorously validate service effectiveness through PoC rather than focusing solely on revenue performance. Their goal is to enter the global market by delivering high-quality services. In this process, they aim to become a unicorn in the AI math education market by sincerely seeking international investors who understand Procyan’s vision and goals, irrespective of nationality.

Regarding their participation in CES, a Procyan representative stated, “Procyan’s purpose in participating in CES 2024 is to clearly show the world that our goal is not just to lead the ‘market’ through math education but to lead the ‘world.’ Our slogan is ‘A Better World Through Mathematics,’ and we have a vision to produce quality talents through math education for the betterment of the world. Companies participating in CES must have global standard business goals and ideas. Through CES, we hope to discover partners and investors who align with our vision and goals and become an innovation icon in the global education industry.
